extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities (e.g., PAK Solutions), state air agencies (NHDES), EPA staff, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register proposed rule describing EPA's proposed approval of a New Hampshire SIP revision that incorporates a State-issued RACT Order for PAK Solutions, including the compliance, monitoring, recordkeeping, DERs, and comment procedures relevant to the action. Useful for regulated facilities, state agencies, and members of the public who will submit comments or implement the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment receipt deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments must be received on or before February 22, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments submitted after this date will not be considered. See the DATES section for the official deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission methods and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments identified by Docket ID No. EPA-R01-OAR-2023-0576 at https://www.regulations.gov, or via email to Patrick Lillis at lillis.patrick@epa.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For comments submitted at Regulations.gov, follow the online instructions; once submitted, comments cannot be edited or removed. The EPA may publish any comment received to its public docket. Do not submit electronically any information you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute. Multimedia submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written comment; the written comment is considered the official comment and should include discussion of all points you wish to make. The EPA will generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing system). For additional submission methods, contact the person identified in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT section. For full guidance see https://www.epa.gov/dockets/commenting-epa-dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public docket availability and inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly available docket materials are available at https://www.regulations.gov or at the U.S. EPA Region 1 Regional Office, Air and Radiation Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA requests that, if possible, you contact the person listed in FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT to schedule your inspection. The Regional Office's official hours are Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., excluding legal holidays and facility closures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Env-A 1215 VOC control standards
rubrics_metrics.description: PAK Solutions shall comply with the VOC control standards specified in Env-A 1215 Rotogravure and Flexographic Printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RACT Order requires compliance with the specific capture and control requirements in Env-A 1215 for the facility's rotogravure and flexographic printing operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture and reduction performance thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture and control system performance must meet the 60% capture and 90% reduction requirement specified in Env-A 1215.03(b) and Env-A 1215.04(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order contemplates use of alternative compliance (DERs) only for periods when the RTO cannot meet these thresholds due to malfunction or routine maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: RTO monitoring, testing, and maintenance obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: PAK shall conduct monitoring and testing activities of the RTO and operate and maintain equipment to continuously monitor the temperature of the combustion chamber of the RTO; maintain the RTO consistent with the manufacturer's recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records of control device monitoring and maintenance must be maintained on site and submitted upon request. Continuous temperature monitoring is required to demonstrate operation of the control device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and generation of Discrete Emissions Reductions (DERs)
rubrics_metrics.description: PAK may generate and use DERs in order to comply with the VOC reduction requirements during periods when the RTO is shut down due to maintenance or malfunction, and may generate DERs for VOC emission reductions that exceed the reductions specified in the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAK is allowed to use DERs for RACT compliance and is allowed to sell DERs to other entities within the State of New Hampshire. Use and generation of DERs must follow the instructions in RACT Order RO-0007 and the referenced state rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: DERs recordkeeping and annual reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PAK must maintain sufficient recordkeeping and timely annual reporting related to DERs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAK is required to submit an annual report to NHDES on the projected use of credits (DERs) for the upcoming calendar year by November 30th (requirements outlined in Env-A 3104.08). PAK must also submit an annual report by April 15th to NHDES on the balance of credits (DERs) for the previous calendar year (requirements outlined in Env-A 3103.08 and Env-A 3104.09).

rubrics_metrics.name: On-site records and SIP Env-A 900 obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Records are required to be maintained on site and submitted upon request for control device monitoring and maintenance; PAK is subject to the applicable recordkeeping and reporting requirements of SIP‑approved Env-A 900.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Env-A 900 requires annual reporting to the state of emissions data and other information relating to compliance. Any additional recordkeeping requirements are outlined within Table 5 in the state's permit to operate; additional reporting requirements are outlined in Table 6 of the permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA SIP approval legal standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Clean Air Act, the Administrator is required to approve a SIP submission that complies with the provisions of the Act and applicable Federal regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's role is to approve state choices provided they meet the criteria of the Clean Air Act (see 42 U.S.C. 7410(k); 40 CFR 52.02(a)). This proposed action approves state law as meeting Federal requirements and does not impose additional requirements beyond state law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposes to incorporate by reference RACT Order RO-0007 dated December 14, 2022, into a final EPA rule in accordance with requirements of 1 CFR 51.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA has made, and will continue to make, these documents generally available through https://www.regulations.gov and at the EPA Region 1 Office (contact person in FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT for more information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and Executive Order review determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed approval is accompanied by statutory/EO certifications and determinations about regulatory and economic impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, the action: is not a significant regulatory action under EO 12866 and 13563; does not impose an information collection burden under the Paperwork Reduction Act; is certified as not having a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the Regulatory Flexibility Act; does not contain any unfunded mandate or significantly or uniquely affect small governments under the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act; does not have federalism implications per EO 13132; is not an economically significant regulatory action based on health or safety risks under EO 13045; is not a significant regulatory action under EO 13211; is not subject to Section 12(d) of the NTTAA; and the SIP is not approved to apply on any Indian reservation land or other area where a tribe has jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental justice (EJ) considerations statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The New Hampshire DES did not evaluate environmental justice considerations as part of its SIP submittal; EPA did not perform an EJ analysis and did not consider EJ in this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA states consideration of EJ is not required as part of this action and there is no information in the record inconsistent with E.O. 12898's goal. EPA expects a neutral to positive impact on air quality of the affected area.
